full_judgment: 3. Defendant Nos. 11 and 12 also contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the case of the plaintiffs stating, inter alia, that Rup Chand, son of Obhiram Sarder, the original owner, and his other co-sharers had settled the suit land on 17-5-39 in favour of plaintiffs-predecessor Arjun Mondal and others and that the landlords also got a rent decree for arrears of rent in Rent Suit No. 676 of 1941 from the Court of Munsif, First Court, Khulna and in execution of the decree in Rent Execution Case No. 827 of 1941 the suit land was sold in auction on 16-9-41 which was confirmed on 11-11-41 and the auction purchaser got the writ of delivery of possession on 26-11-41. Thereafter plaintiffs-predecessor. Chandrakanta filed Misc. Case No. 275 of 1941 for setting aside the aforesaid auction sale which was dismissed on 7-3-42 and Misc. Appeal No. 69 of 1942 filed by said Chandra Kanta was also dismissed by the learned District Judge, Khulna on 26-5-42. Thereafter Jogeswar Mondal, another predecessor of the plaintiffs, also filed Misc. Case No. 171 of 1942 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Khulna under section 173(3) of the Bengal Tenancy Act which was also dismissed on 10-2-43. They also denied the plaintiffs are the heirs of Arjun Mondal. According to them, Fakir Mondal died after the auction sale and they claimed the suit land by inheritance.
